t: The primary purpose of a liability insurance policy is to indemnify the insured against:
o: Damage to the insured's own property
Bodily injury suffered by the insured
Legal liability to third parties for damages and costs
Loss of profits following an accident
e: Liability insurance is third-party cover: it pays the damages (and defence costs) the insured becomes legally liable to pay to others. Own property, own injury and loss of profit are first-party exposures covered by other classes.

topic: Law of Torts and Legal Liability
t: The 'neighbour principle', which laid the foundation of the modern law of negligence, was enunciated in:
o: Donoghue v Stevenson (1932)
Rylands v Fletcher (1868)
Hedley Byrne v Heller (1964)
M.C. Mehta v Union of India (1987)
e: Lord Atkin in Donoghue v Stevenson held that one must take reasonable care to avoid acts likely to injure one's 'neighbour'. Rylands concerns strict liability, Hedley Byrne negligent misstatement, and M.C. Mehta absolute liability.

t: The Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991 was enacted in India largely as a consequence of:
o: The Chernobyl nuclear accident
The Exxon Valdez oil spill
The Uphaar cinema fire
The Bhopal gas tragedy of 1984
e: The Bhopal disaster exposed the absence of a mechanism for immediate relief to victims of hazardous-industry accidents, leading to the no-fault relief scheme of the PLI Act, 1991.

t: In the Indian public liability (non-industrial risks) policy, the insurer's maximum liability is expressed as:
o: A limit per person and per accident
Any One Accident (AOA) and Any One Year (AOY) limits
A sum insured on the insured's property
A first-loss limit on turnover
e: Indian public liability policies carry an AOA limit for any one accident and an AOY aggregate limit for the policy year, chosen in a ratio such as 1:1 to 1:4.

t: The products liability policy issued in the Indian market is normally written on:
o: An occurrence basis without any retroactive date
A claims-made basis with a retroactive date
A losses-occurring-during basis
A discovery basis with unlimited reporting period
e: Indian products liability cover responds to claims first made against the insured during the policy period for injury/damage occurring after the retroactive date, limiting the long tail for the insurer.

topic: Employers' Liability and Employees' Compensation Insurance
t: The Employees' Compensation Act, 1923 was earlier known as:
o: The Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923, renamed by the 2009 amendment with effect from 2010
The Fatal Accidents Act, 1855
The Factories Act, 1948
The Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948
e: The Workmen's Compensation (Amendment) Act, 2009 substituted 'employee' for 'workman' and renamed the statute; it came into force in January 2010.

t: Coverage A of the ISO Commercial General Liability (CGL) form provides cover for:
o: Bodily injury and property damage liability
Personal and advertising injury liability
Medical payments regardless of fault
Product recall expenses
e: Coverage A is the core BI/PD liability section; Coverage B deals with personal and advertising injury and Coverage C with medical payments. Recall is excluded from the CGL.

t: The form of reinsurance most commonly used to protect a liability portfolio against large individual claims is:
o: Quota share treaty only
Facultative placement of every policy
Stop loss treaty
Excess of loss treaty
e: Liability losses are severity-driven and unpredictable in size, so cedants buy per-risk/per-event excess of loss protection above a retention rather than sharing every policy proportionally.

topic: Law of Torts and Legal Liability
t: The maxim 'res ipsa loquitur' in a negligence action means that:
o: The defendant is strictly liable irrespective of fault
The plaintiff must prove every element of negligence
The claim is barred by limitation
The facts themselves raise an inference of negligence, shifting the burden to the defendant to explain
e: Where an accident would not ordinarily happen without negligence and the thing was under the defendant's control, the 'thing speaks for itself' and the defendant must rebut the presumption.

t: Under the Schedule to the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991, the relief payable for a fatal accident (in addition to reimbursement of medical expenses) is:
e: The Act provides no-fault relief of ₹25,000 per fatal accident plus reimbursement of medical expenses up to ₹12,500; the same ₹25,000 figure applies to permanent total disability.

topic: Employers' Liability and Employees' Compensation Insurance
t: The minimum compensation payable for death of an employee under the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923 (as amended in 2009) is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Death compensation is 50% of wages × relevant factor or ₹1,20,000, whichever is more; the corresponding minimum for permanent total disablement is ₹1,40,000.

t: The ratios of AOA to AOY limits generally available under Indian public liability policies are:
o: 1:1 only
Unlimited AOY against a fixed AOA
e: The insured selects an AOA limit and an AOY limit of one to four times the AOA; premium is loaded for higher ratios.

t: The 'vendors' liability' extension to a products liability policy:
o: Extends indemnity to distributors and retailers selling the insured's products as additional insureds
Covers the cost of recalling defective products from vendors
Covers claims that the product failed to perform as promised
Covers inherent vice of the goods during storage
e: Vendors' cover protects those in the distribution chain for claims arising from the insured's product, usually for a named list of vendors; recall and efficacy remain excluded.

t: In a claims-made professional indemnity policy, the 'retroactive date' is:
o: The date on which the current policy expires
The date before which acts or omissions giving rise to a claim are not covered
The date on which the claim is first made
The date on which the first premium is paid
e: Cover applies only to professional work performed on or after the retroactive date, usually the inception of the first uninterrupted claims-made policy.

topic: Employers' Liability and Employees' Compensation Insurance
t: Under the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923 the employer must, in addition to compensation for death, pay funeral expenses of not less than:
e: Section 4(4), as amended in 2009, provides for funeral expenses of ₹5,000 to be deposited with the Commissioner along with the death compensation.

t: The purpose of the 'insured versus insured' exclusion in a D&O policy is to:
o: Exclude claims arising from fraud of a director
Exclude securities claims against the company
Prevent collusive claims brought by the company or one insured against other insured directors
Exclude claims by regulators
e: The exclusion stops the company from recovering business losses from its own insurer by suing its directors; carve-backs usually exist for derivative shareholder suits and whistle-blower claims.

t: A products liability policy is rated at ₹0.50 per mille of turnover. The insured's annual turnover is ₹200 crore. The basic premium is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). ₹200 crore × 0.50/1000 = ₹2,00,00,00,000 × 0.0005 = ₹10,00,000.

t: Coverage C (Medical Payments) of the CGL policy pays medical expenses:
o: Only if the insured is held legally liable
Only for injuries to the insured's employees
Only after a lawsuit has been filed
Regardless of fault for bodily injury to third parties on the insured's premises or arising from its operations, if expenses are incurred within one year
e: Med-pay is a goodwill, no-fault cover with a small per-person limit; it excludes the insured's employees and injuries falling within the products-completed operations hazard.

topic: Cyber and Other Specialised Liability Covers
t: Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 the maximum monetary penalty that can be imposed for failure to take reasonable security safeguards is:
o: ₹250 crore
₹50 crore
₹500 crore
₹5 crore
e: The Schedule to the DPDP Act prescribes a penalty of up to ₹250 crore per instance for breach of the obligation to take reasonable security safeguards; this is a key driver of cyber liability exposure.

t: The main difficulty that liability business poses for a reinsurer, compared with property business, is that:
o: Losses are settled within the policy year
Claims inflation is absent
The premium is known with certainty
Claims are reported and settled years after the policy period, requiring large IBNR reserves
e: Liability is a long-tail class: latent injury and litigation mean the reinsurer must reserve for incurred-but-not-reported losses long after the treaty year.

t: Which of the following is a third-party insurance?
o: A standard fire policy on a factory building
A public liability policy
A personal accident policy
A marine cargo policy
e: Only the public liability policy pays for losses suffered by persons other than the insured; the others indemnify the insured's own property or person.

topic: Law of Torts and Legal Liability
t: The rule in Rylands v Fletcher imposes:
o: Fault-based liability requiring proof of negligence
Vicarious liability of an employer
Strict liability for escape of a dangerous thing brought on to land in a non-natural use
No liability for escape of water
e: Liability arises without proof of negligence once the dangerous thing escapes and causes damage, subject to defences such as act of God, act of a stranger and statutory authority.

t: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (as revised by the 2021 Rules), a District Commission can entertain complaints where the value of goods or services paid does not exceed:
o: ₹1 crore
₹20 lakh
₹50 lakh
₹2 crore
e: The 2021 Rules fixed the District Commission limit at ₹50 lakh, the State Commission between ₹50 lakh and ₹2 crore, and the National Commission above ₹2 crore.

t: A public liability policy has an AOA limit of ₹1 crore and an AOY limit of ₹3 crore. During the year four accidents give rise to admitted liabilities of ₹80 lakh, ₹1.2 crore, ₹90 lakh and ₹60 lakh. Ignoring excess, the total amount payable by the insurer is:
o: ₹3.5 crore
₹3 crore
₹3.3 crore
₹2.7 crore
e: The second accident is capped at the AOA of ₹1 crore, giving ₹80L + ₹1cr + ₹90L + ₹60L = ₹3.3 crore, which is then capped at the AOY aggregate of ₹3 crore.

t: Hedley Byrne v Heller (1964) is important for professional liability because it established:
o: Liability for negligent misstatement causing pure economic loss where a special relationship exists
Strict liability of manufacturers for defective products
The employer's common-law duty to provide a safe system of work
Absolute liability of hazardous industries
e: The case recognised that a professional who gives advice knowing it will be relied upon owes a duty of care, making financial-loss claims against accountants, bankers and advisers actionable.

topic: Employers' Liability and Employees' Compensation Insurance
t: A workman aged 40 (relevant factor 184.17) drawing monthly wages of ₹18,000 dies in an accident arising out of employment. Taking the notified wage ceiling of ₹15,000, the compensation payable under the Employees' Compensation Act is:
e: Death compensation = 50% of monthly wages (capped at ₹15,000) × relevant factor = 7,500 × 184.17 = ₹13,81,275, which exceeds the statutory minimum of ₹1,20,000.

t: A CGL policy has an each-occurrence limit of ₹2 crore and a general aggregate of ₹5 crore. Three covered occurrences in the year produce losses of ₹2.5 crore, ₹1.5 crore and ₹1.8 crore. The insurer pays in total:
o: ₹5.8 crore
₹5 crore
₹5.3 crore
₹4 crore
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). First loss limited to ₹2 cr, second ₹1.5 cr (total ₹3.5 cr), third limited by the remaining aggregate of ₹1.5 cr, giving ₹5 crore in all.

t: Section 197(13) of the Companies Act, 2013 provides that the premium paid by a company for D&O insurance:
o: Is not treated as part of the director's remuneration unless the director is proved guilty of the misconduct insured against
Cannot be paid by the company at all
Is always treated as managerial remuneration
Can be paid only for independent directors
e: The section expressly allows companies to insure KMP against negligence, default, breach of duty etc.; the premium becomes remuneration only if the person is proved guilty.

t: In the CGL policy, 'occurrence' is defined as:
o: A single sudden and identifiable event only
A written demand for damages
An accident, including continuous or repeated exposure to substantially the same general harmful conditions
Any deliberate act of the insured
e: The definition extends beyond sudden events to gradual exposure (e.g. slow leakage), while the expected or intended injury exclusion removes deliberate acts.

topic: Cyber and Other Specialised Liability Covers
t: A carriers' legal liability policy covers the liability of a goods transporter for loss of or damage to goods carried. In India this liability is currently governed by:
o: The Carriers Act, 1865, which is still in force
The Carriage by Road Act, 2007
The Sale of Goods Act, 1930
The Indian Railways Act, 1989
e: The Carriage by Road Act, 2007 repealed the Carriers Act, 1865 and now regulates common carriers of goods by road, including registration and liability for loss.

topic: Underwriting and Claims in Liability Insurance
t: In Indian public and products liability policies, defence costs incurred with the insurer's consent are normally:
o: Payable in addition to the limit of indemnity without any cap
Included within the limit of indemnity (costs inclusive)
Excluded altogether
Payable only if the insured wins the case
e: Indian liability wordings are 'costs inclusive': legal costs and expenses erode the AOA/AOY limit, unlike the ISO CGL where supplementary payments are outside the limits.

t: A 'clash cover' in liability reinsurance protects the cedant when:
o: A single policy is shared on a quota share basis
The annual loss ratio exceeds an agreed percentage
One event triggers losses under several of its policies or classes, exceeding the retention in aggregate
A single large risk is placed facultatively
e: Clash (per-event) excess of loss responds to accumulation across policies from one occurrence, e.g. an explosion injuring workers, visitors and neighbours insured under different covers.

t: Liability insurance is described as 'long-tail' business because:
o: A long time can elapse between the event causing injury and final settlement of the claim
Limits of indemnity are very large
It is bought by a large number of insureds
It contains a long list of exclusions
e: Latent injuries, delayed discovery and protracted litigation mean liabilities may crystallise years after the policy period, complicating reserving and pricing.

topic: Law of Torts and Legal Liability
t: An employer is vicariously liable for a tort committed by an employee when the tort is committed:
o: While the employee is committing a serious crime for personal gain
While the employee is on leave
By an independent contractor engaged by the employer
In the course of the employee's employment
e: Vicarious liability attaches to acts done within the scope of employment, even if done improperly; it generally does not extend to independent contractors or to a 'frolic of his own'.

t: Under Section 3 of the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991, a claimant seeking relief is NOT required to prove:
o: Any wrongful act, neglect or default of the owner
That an accident occurred
That death or injury resulted
That a hazardous substance was being handled
e: Section 3 imposes no-fault liability on the owner; the claimant must only establish the accident involving the hazardous substance and the resulting injury or damage.

t: The minimum paid-up equity capital required to start a life or general insurance company in India is:
o: ₹50 crore
₹100 crore
₹200 crore
₹500 crore
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). ₹100 crore for a direct insurer; ₹200 crore for a reinsurer (Section 6 of the Insurance Act).

t: For the purpose of Indian public liability policies, which of the following is treated as an 'industrial' risk?
o: A five-star hotel
A manufacturing unit, factory or godown
A school
A cinema hall
e: Manufacturing premises, warehouses and godowns are rated under the industrial public liability policy, while hotels, offices, schools and cinemas fall under the non-industrial policy.

t: Products exported to the USA or Canada are, under a standard Indian products liability policy:
o: Automatically covered within the territorial limits
Covered without additional premium
Permanently excluded with no option to cover
Excluded unless specifically agreed and endorsed at additional premium, because of the litigious environment and high awards there
e: North American exposure is excluded as standard; insurers may grant it with higher premium, higher excess and sometimes a claims-made and reported restriction.

t: An 'extended reporting period' (discovery period) in a claims-made PI policy:
o: Extends the policy period to cover new acts of negligence
Increases the limit of indemnity
Allows claims made after expiry, for acts before expiry, to be reported when cover is not renewed
Moves the retroactive date forward
e: When a professional retires or the insurer does not renew, the ERP preserves cover for claims notified during the extended period arising from pre-expiry work.

topic: Employers' Liability and Employees' Compensation Insurance
t: Table B of the Indian Workmen's/Employees' Compensation insurance policy provides indemnity for the employer's liability under:
o: The Employees' Compensation Act only
The Employees' Compensation Act and common law
The Fatal Accidents Act, 1855 and common law only, excluding the EC Act
The ESI Act
e: Table A covers EC Act, Fatal Accidents Act and common-law liability; Table B is for employees not covered by the EC Act and responds to Fatal Accidents Act and common-law claims only.

t: Which of the following is typically EXCLUDED under a D&O policy?
o: Costs of responding to a regulatory investigation
Defence costs for an alleged breach of duty
Claims for wrongful termination of an employee
Loss arising from deliberate fraud or dishonesty established by final adjudication
e: Fraud and illegal personal profit are excluded, but only once established by judgment or admission so that defence costs are advanced until then; the other items are commonly covered.

t: The liquor liability exclusion in the CGL policy applies to:
o: Any insured who serves alcohol at an office party
Insureds in the business of manufacturing, distributing, selling, serving or furnishing alcoholic beverages
All restaurants, whether or not they serve alcohol
No insured, as liquor liability is covered in full
e: 'Host liquor' liability of non-liquor businesses remains covered; those in the liquor business must buy a separate Liquor Liability policy.

topic: Cyber and Other Specialised Liability Covers
t: The CERT-In directions of April 2022 require Indian entities to report cyber security incidents within:
o: 6 hours of noticing the incident
24 hours
72 hours
7 days
e: The directions mandate reporting within six hours, a much shorter window than the 72 hours under GDPR, which increases incident response and notification cost exposure.

topic: Underwriting and Claims in Liability Insurance
t: The rating factors MOST relevant in pricing a public liability policy are:
o: Number of employees and their wages
Value of the building
Sum insured on stocks
Turnover, nature of the business and the limits of indemnity selected
e: Premium is computed on annual turnover at a rate reflecting the hazard class of the business and loaded for the AOA/AOY limits and ratio; wages are the EC policy rating base.

t: The percentage of obligatory cession to GIC Re applicable to Indian general insurers since financial year 2022-23 is:
e: IRDAI reduced the obligatory cession from 5% to 4% with effect from 1 April 2022, and this level has continued for subsequent years.

t: The control level of solvency ratio that every insurer must maintain is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Available solvency margin must be at least 150% of the required solvency margin; falling below triggers IRDAI action.

t: Pollution and contamination under the Indian public liability policy are:
o: Excluded unless caused by a sudden, unintended and unexpected happening during the policy period
Always covered including gradual seepage
Covered only for gradual pollution
Covered including fines and clean-up ordered by the regulator
e: Only sudden and accidental pollution is covered; gradual pollution and government-imposed fines require a separate environmental impairment liability policy.

t: Products liability generally arises from injury or damage occurring:
o: On the insured's own premises during manufacture
Away from the insured's premises after the product has left the insured's custody or control
During the manufacturing process only
Only during transit of the goods
e: Once the product is sold and handed over, accidents caused by it elsewhere constitute the products hazard; accidents on the premises during operations fall under public liability.

topic: Underwriting and Claims in Liability Insurance
t: A claims-made policy for 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026 has a retroactive date of 1 April 2020. An act of negligence occurred in January 2023 and the claim is first made in August 2025. Is the claim covered?
o: No, because the act occurred before the policy period
Yes, because the act occurred after the retroactive date and the claim was made within the policy period
Only if the policy were on an occurrence basis
No, because the retroactive date must coincide with policy inception
e: The claims-made trigger is the date the claim is made; acts after the retroactive date are within cover even though they predate the current policy.

t: Under Section 7A of the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991, every owner taking out insurance must also contribute to the Environment Relief Fund an amount equal to:
o: The premium paid for the policy
10% of the premium
₹1 lakh
The AOA limit of the policy
e: The 1992 amendment created the ERF; the insurer collects a contribution equal to the premium along with the premium and remits it to the Fund, which pays relief beyond the policy limits.
